# dsh-resizable-settings
English | 中文
Makes the Settings dialog that opens from the settings button **resizable by dragging its edges and
corners**, and **movable by dragging its top strip**.
## Interaction
| Action | Where |

| Change the width | Left/right edge (a 6px band just inside the panel) |
| Change the height | Top/

bottom edge |
| Change both | The four corners (16×16) |
| Move it elsewhere | The panel's **top 20p

x strip** (the empty space above the header) |
| Restore the default size and position | **Press twi

ty space above the header) |
| Restore the default size and position | **Press twice** on any band |
Hovering an edge turns the pointer into the matching resize cursor and lights up a thin line, so the
handles are easy to find.
The draggable area stops at the **bottom of DSH's top bar**: the panel's top edge can go no higher t
han the caption's lower edge, so it can never be dragged into the top bar and get stuck there.
Size and position are remembered — across the next open, and across an app restart.
## How it works
The dialog is rendered by `ui-settings-general` as a modal panel with `role="dialog" aria-modal="tru
e"`, inside a fixed, flex-centred overlay; the panel itself is hard-coded to `width:800px` and has n
o resize affordance.
A few things have to be exactly right:
- **The handles must be drawn inside the panel.** The panel is `overflow:hidden`, so handles drawn o

utside its box are clipped — invisible and unclickable.
- **Freeze the panel before dragging.** Flex
centring means growing it expands both sides at once, so the first press converts the panel to `pos
ition:absolute` with explicit `left/top/width/height` taken from its current `getBoundingClientRect(

)`. After that **the grabbed edge follows the pointer while the opposite edge stays put**.
- **The c
eiling is the viewport, not a constant.** Dragging east grows until "the right edge reaches the view
port margin"; the ceiling depends on where the left edge is. That way a drag can never push the pane

l off screen, and hitting the ceiling never makes the anchored edge jump.
- **The top boundary is th
e lower edge of DSH's top bar, not the top of the viewport.** On Windows the caption is a 40px `-web
kit-app-region: drag` strip, and the caption menubar host sits at `z-index:1100`, **above this modal
's `1000`** — a pointer landing on that strip is consumed by window dragging or the menubar and neve
r reaches the panel. So once the panel parks there, its top move grip never receives a `pointerdown`
again (the cursor does not change either): the panel is effectively pinned and cannot be dragged ba
ck out. The floor comes from DSH's own `--dsh-frame-chrome-top` (the caption height, zeroed in nativ
e fullscreen); macOS has no such strip and uses `--dsh-frame-top-clearance` instead. A plain browser

document publishes neither, so it falls back to the 12px margin.
- **The right handle is inset 6px.
** The settings scroller owns the outermost 5px (`--dsh-scrollbar-width`); covering it would turn "d

rag the scrollbar" into "resize".

Then restart DSH Desktop.
## Tests
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The harness implements just enough of `getBoundingClientRect`, `style` and `pointerdown/move/up`, ru
ns the real bundle, and asserts the **resize arithmetic** line by line: each of the four edges only
affects its own axis, a south-east drag leaves the origin alone, a north-west drag moves the origin
and shrinks, the minimum-size floor, the ceiling following the viewport and the anchored edge, the a
nchored edge holding still when a drag hits the floor, moves clamped by the viewport, double-press r
eset, restore on reopen, and teardown.
The top-bar floor has its own cases: with no top bar the move grip still reaches the 12px margin, wi
th a 40px top bar it stops at 40px, a north drag cannot push the panel back into the top bar, and a
box stored inside the top bar is pulled back below it on the next open.
## Package layout
| Path | Purpose |

| `lib/client.js` | The browser half: all the logic lives here, hand-written rather than built |
| `
lib/index.js` | The host half: an empty implementation that exists only so the plugin owns a Loader

row |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | The bundle patch, pointed at by `dsh.bundle.patch` in `package.json` |
| `locale/*.json` | The title and description shown in the plugin list (`meta.title` / `meta.descrip

tion`) |
| `test/resize.test.mjs` | The offline harness |
`locale/` has two easy-to-miss constraints. DSH treats `locale/en.json` as the **anchor**: if it can
not be read, no language file in that directory is read at all (so the English one must exist). File
names must be language ids (`en`, `zh`, `zh-CN`). And the files are fetched through Node's ESM reso
lver, so they must be allowed in `package.json`'s `exports` (`"./locale/*.json"`) and listed in `fil
es` to reach the published package — missing either does not raise an error, it just falls back to t
he English description in the list.
## Limits
- It only touches the Settings modal (`[role="dialog"][aria-modal="true"]` whose class contains `_pa

nel`). Other dialogs are unaffected.
- The panel's own layout, behaviour and shortcuts are unchanged

; it only gains draggable edges and a top strip.
- The size is stored in the browser's `localStorage

` (key `dsh-resizable-settings.v1`), independently per machine and browser.
- If a DSH upgrade chang
es the settings panel's structure (no longer `role="dialog"` plus an inline `_panel` class), the han
dles will not find the panel and the plugin silently does nothing — it raises no error and does not
break the settings page.
